item.title: A Retrospective Review of Emergency Department Coronavirus 2019 Cases vs. County-Wide Cases to Demonstrate a Temporal Correlation
item.description:
Background: To better prepare for future Coronavirus 2019 (COVID-19) variants, new forms of surveillance are necessary to predict outbreaks and prepare communities and hospitals.

Objectives: We examined the temporal correlation between emergency department (ED) and county COVID-19 cases and determine if ED COVID-19 trends can serve as an indicator to predict county-level outbreaks.

Methods: A retrospective analysis of COVID-19 data from March 2020 to April 2023 was conducted, comparing hospital COVID-19 positive cases to local county positive cases. Data were analyzed using two metrics: a positivity cutoff and a cross-correlation analysis. We set the positivity cutoff (percent of positive tests to total tests) at 4% threshold based on guidelines from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and identified dates when ED and county positivity surpassed this threshold. The cross-correlation analysis between the county and the ED determined the time lag interval (in days) that had the strongest correlation between daily ED and county positive case volume per outbreak.

Results: There were both seven ED and county dates that met the positivity cutoff but only five that corresponded to the same outbreaks. The county outbreaks preceded ED outbreaks, ranging from 2 to 59 days, with a mean of 42 days prior. The cross-correlational analysis underwent an additional sensitivity analysis, resulting in an R-squared value ranging 0.8435-0.9271, averaging 8.25 days of county precedence.

Conclusion: ED data is not a suitable predictor of county-level COVID-19 cases; however, the strong correlation of county precedence can prove helpful to prepare hospitals for future outbreaks.

Fu B, Theiling BJ, Hanlin ER, Limkakeng AT

item.title: Sex and Age-Based Effect on Outcomes in the Setting of Traumatic Hemorrhage
item.description:
Background: Survival differences between injured females and males have been demonstrated.

Study objectives: To analyze trauma survival stratified by sex and age for a given transfusion volume.

Methods: The Trauma Quality Improvement Program registry was analyzed from 2020 to 2023. Patients ≥15 years who received any volume of blood products within 4 hours were included.

Results: There were 13,987 patients (3165/13,987, 22.6% female) who received 75-600 mL/kg of all blood products within the first 4 hours of admission, i.e., the range where a difference in cumulative 24-hour survival between males and females was observed. In this range, the cumulative probability of 24-hour survival was lower for females compared to males (46 vs. 51%, respectively). This difference was not observed in the adjusted analysis (odds ratio 0.93, 95% confidence interval 0.84-1.02). In the unadjusted age and sex subanalysis, females >50 years had the highest mortality of any of the four groups of patients once ∼100 mL/kg of blood products had been transfused. Both males and females aged 15-50 years had the lowest mortality for any volume of transfusion; males >50 years had intermediate mortality. In the regression analysis performed on patients who received a total volume of 100-600 mL/kg of transfusion, 15- to 50-year-old males had significantly lower 24-hour survival compared to similarly aged females. There was no difference in this parameter between the females and males who were >50 years.

Conclusion: Adjusting for differences did not reveal a difference in overall survival between males and females; younger males had lower survival compared to similarly aged females.

Yazer MH, Schauer SG

item.title: A Novel Governance Model for Real-Time Clinical Decision-Making in Viral Hemorrhagic Fever Outbreaks: Ethiopia's 2025 Marburg Virus Disease Response
item.description:
Background: In November 2025, Ethiopia declared its first Marburg Virus Disease outbreak. With no licensed vaccines or specific therapeutics, the Ministry of Health established a novel dual-advisory governance structure for case management.

Objectives: This case study examines the development, implementation, and associated outcomes of Ethiopia's dual-advisory governance model during the 2025 Marburg outbreak.

Methods: We conducted a qualitative case study using thematic synthesis of official government documents, meeting minutes, and clinical logs from November 13, 2025, to January 26, 2026. The Ministry of Health granted access; all patient data were anonymized.

Results: The dual-advisory model comprised two parallel bodies: a strategic Technical Working Group for national guideline development, and a tactical National Advisory Team providing daily consultation to frontline clinicians. A ``morning meeting'' mechanism enabled bidirectional communication. During the response, Remdesivir was deployed within 6 days (278 post-exposure prophylaxis [PEP] courses, 10 treatment courses); monoclonal antibody MBP091 was operationalized within 8 days. The outbreak resulted in 14 confirmed cases, five survivors, and three healthcare worker infections (two deceased).

Conclusions: Ethiopia's dual-advisory governance model demonstrated the ability to bridge strategic planning and tactical clinical action. The separation of functions, institutionalized daily communication, and links to resource mobilization represent potentially transferable principles for outbreak governance. However, as a descriptive case study, observed outcomes cannot be attributed to the model, and further evaluation is needed.

Waganew W, Safewo A, Buno E, Worku A, Eshetu A, Amogne W

item.title: Between the Siren and the Silence
Evaluating Culturally Tailored Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) Training in Racial and Ethnically Diverse Communities
item.description:
Background: Bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is a critical determinant of survival following out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). However, racial and ethnic minority populations in the United States are less likely to receive bystander CPR and experience disproportionately poorer outcomes.

Study objectives: The objective of this study was to pilot and evaluate the feasibility of a culturally tailored hands-only CPR curriculum and assess changes in self-reported confidence and perceived difficulty of CPR among Indian American, Chinese American, and African American participants.

Methods: We conducted a single-cohort pre-post study among three groups. Community-specific focus groups informed cultural adaptations to a standard emergency services hands-only CPR curriculum, and trainings were delivered at Hindu temples, Chinese language schools, and African American churches. Primary outcomes, measured by 10-point Likert scales, were changes in confidence in four main CPR skills and perceived difficulty of CPR.

Results: The study included 104 participants: 47 (45%) Indian American, 23 (22%) Chinese American, and 34 (33%) African American participants. Confidence increased across the four main CPR skills, with the largest improvements observed in the connect an automated external defibrillator (AED) skill (+4.5; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.80-5.22). Perceived difficulty of CPR also decreased (-2.65; 95% CI: 1.97-3.33).

Conclusion: This pilot study provides preliminary evidence for the feasibility and acceptability of culturally tailored hands-only CPR training in community settings, with participants reporting improved confidence and reduced perceived difficulty of CPR after training. These exploratory findings warrant further evaluation in adequately powered comparative studies to determine whether cultural tailoring offers benefit beyond standard CPR instruction for racial and ethnic minority communities and can contribute to reducing disparities in cardiac arrest outcomes.

Sivashankar S, Shirolkar P, Blewer A, Chen A, Monk L, Lu M

item.title: Epidemiology of Nephrolithiasis Among United States Emergency Departments Over a 9-Year Period
item.description:
Background: Nephrolithiasis is a common emergency department (ED) presentation, yet contemporary national data on management trends are limited.

Objectives: To characterize recent trends in diagnostic evaluation, management, and disposition for adult ED patients with nephrolithiasis.

Methods: This cross-sectional study analyzed United States ED encounters from January 1, 2016 to December 31, 2024 using the Epic Cosmos database, including all adult patients (≥18 years) with an ICD-10 diagnosis of nephrolithiasis. Outcomes included hospital admission, imaging utilization, urine culture collection, medication administration, discharge prescription, and procedural intervention. Descriptive statistics were utilized to characterize the study population. To account for the longitudinal expansion of the database, time-stratified odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using the general ED population as a background comparator. Significance of temporal shifts was assessed using Cochran-Armitage tests.

Results: Of 248,564,812 ED encounters, 2,762,879 (1.1%) were for nephrolithiasis. Hospital admission rates increased from 8.9% in 2016 to 12.7% in 2024. Computed tomography (CT) utilization increased (73.8-89.8%), outpacing general ED trends (OR 27.2-45.6), while ultrasound declined (5.8-3.8%). In the ED, opioid use fell (61.5-49.7%), exceeding background reductions (OR 6.6-4.8), while ketorolac was the most common analgesic administered (61.6%). Tamsulosin remained the top discharge prescription (47.2%). Procedural interventions were uncommon, though stent placement increased from 3.0% to 6.8%.

Conclusions: We identified rising hospital admission rates and an increase in CT utilization, while there was a decline in ultrasound. This divergence between practice patterns and evidence-based guidelines, highlights critical opportunities for quality improvement.

Riley GV, Buell KG, Moyer E, Bernard K, Panken EJ, Fantus RJ
